examples.japanese: {歯|は}ブラシを{新|あたら}しいのに{替|か}えた。
examples.english: I replaced my toothbrush with a new one.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}に{歯|は}ブラシを{持|も}っていくのを{忘|わす}れた。
examples.english: I forgot to bring a toothbrush on the trip.

examples.japanese: {電動|でんどう}{歯|は}ブラシは{磨|みが}き{残|のこ}しが{少|すく}ない。
examples.english: Electric toothbrushes leave less residue after brushing.

notes:
A compound of {歯|は} (tooth) and ブラシ (brush, from English). One of the essential daily hygiene items in Japanese households.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {歯|は}を{磨|みが}く: to brush one's teeth
- {歯|は}ブラシを{替|か}える: to replace one's toothbrush
- {歯|は}ブラシで{磨|みが}く: to brush with a toothbrush

RELATED TERMS:
- {歯磨|はみが}き{粉|こ}: toothpaste
- {電動|でんどう}{歯|は}ブラシ: electric toothbrush
- {歯間|しかん}ブラシ: interdental brush
- デンタルフロス / {糸|いと}ようじ: dental floss

USAGE:
In Japan, hotels and inns ({旅館|りょかん}) often provide disposable toothbrushes as amenities. When traveling, {使|つ}い{捨|す}て{歯|は}ブラシ (disposable toothbrush) is a useful term to know.
